problems.title: Turn a squared-sine equation into cosine
problems.question: Solve 2sin²4x=3cos8x+5.
problems.idea: Use the double-angle identity to express both sides in cos8x.

problems.title: A quadratic inequality in cosine
problems.question: Solve 6cos²x-5cosx+1<0.
problems.idea: Factor the quadratic, then use where cosine lies strictly between its two roots.
formulas: Cosine decreases from 1 to -1 on [0,π] and is even and 2π-periodic.
steps: With t=cosx, the product is negative exactly when 1/3<t<1/2.
On the upper half of the unit circle, the solutions are a<x<b. Reflect across 0 for the other interval, then add full turns.
The boundaries are excluded because the original inequality is strict.

problems.title: Cancel a nonzero tangent difference
problems.question: tanx and tany are distinct, tanx=3, and 3tan(x-y)=tanx-tany. Find tan(x+y).
problems.idea: Use the tangent difference formula, then cancel the nonzero difference specified in the question.
steps: Thus t=2/3. The difference denominator is 3, so it is valid.
The sum tangent is (3+2/3)/(1-2)=-11/3. Its denominator is also nonzero.

problems.title: Square a three-cosine product
problems.question: Find the rational value of (cos20°cos40°cos80°)².
problems.idea: Apply the sine double-angle identity three times.
steps: Because sin160°=sin20°≠0, cancel it to get cos20°cos40°cos80°=1/8.

problems.title: Recover two acute angles from weighted sine squares
problems.question: Acute angles x,y satisfy 3sin²x+2sin²y=1 and 3sin²x=2sin²y. Find cos(x+2y).
problems.idea: The two equal weighted terms must each be one-half.
steps: Since y is acute, y=30°, so cos2y=1/2 and sin2y=√3/2.

problems.title: Sign chart for a product of trigonometric functions
problems.question: Solve sin3x cos2x<0.
problems.idea: Find all zeros in one full 2π period and keep intervals where the two factors have opposite signs.
steps: Between consecutive zeros the factors keep their signs. A midpoint sign test gives a negative product on (π/4,π/3), (2π/3,3π/4), (π,5π/4), (4π/3,5π/3), and (7π/4,2π).
All zero endpoints are excluded. Repeat these intervals by adding 2kπ for every integer k.
problems.answer: All five open intervals listed in step 2, repeated by adding 2kπ for any integer k. All endpoints are excluded.

problems.title: Area of a triangular face above a right-triangle base
problems.question: Pyramid MABC has right base ABC, ∠C=90°, AC=3, BC=4. MC is perpendicular to the base and MC=1. Find area MAB.
problems.idea: Use AB as the triangle base. The distance from M to AB combines the pyramid height and the in-plane altitude from C.
formulas: Base area=AC·BC/2=AB·CH/2, where H is the foot from C to AB.
steps: The hypotenuse is AB=5 and the base area is 6, so CH=12/5.
Because MC is perpendicular to the base, MH=√(1+144/25)=13/5.
Also MH is perpendicular to AB, so area MAB=5·(13/5)/2=13/2.

problems.title: A plane through the midpoint of a pyramid’s height
problems.question: A regular square pyramid MABCD has lateral edges making 60° with the base. N is the midpoint of its height. Find the angle between plane CDN and the base.
problems.idea: Take a perpendicular cross-section through the base centre O and the midpoint E of CD.
formulas: For square circumradius R, the centre-to-side distance is r=R/√2.
The angle θ between CDN and the base satisfies tanθ=ON/OE.
steps: Because N bisects the height, ON=h/2=√3R/2.
Both OE and EN are perpendicular to CD, so ∠OEN is the required dihedral angle.

problems.title: Three components of a box diagonal
problems.question: A rectangular box diagonal makes angles x,y with the two lateral face directions, where sinx=1/3 and siny=1/4. Find its angle θ with the base.
problems.idea: The three perpendicular edge components, divided by diagonal length, have squared sum one.
formulas: If diagonal length is d and edge components are a,b,h, then d²=a²+b²+h².
Line-plane sine equals the perpendicular component divided by line length.
steps: The two nonparallel lateral-face planes have perpendicular components a and b, giving a/d=1/3, b/d=1/4 in some order.
problems.note: The two face planes must represent the two different lateral directions; opposite parallel faces provide the same line-plane angle.

problems.title: A cube section with an undefined point
problems.question: A unit cube ABCDA1B1C1D1 is cut by a plane through M,C,D1. Find the section area. The source does not define M.
problems.idea: Show that two admissible choices of M give different areas, so the missing information is essential.
steps: If M=A, the plane is y=x+z. Its section is triangle ACD1: all sides are cube-face diagonals √2, so its area is √3/2.
If M=B, the plane is x+z=1. Its section is rectangle BCD1A1, with sides 1 and √2, giving area √2.
These two valid planes through C,D1 yield different areas. A location or defining condition for M is required for a unique numerical result.
problems.answer: Cannot be determined from the printed data.
problems.note: The original Word document also contains no definition or diagram for M. This is a source omission; the explanation demonstrates why guessing a section area would be unjustified.
